newsitem.title: HUNGARY: K&H Sec rates Danubius as 'buy'.
newsitem.headline: K&H Sec rates Danubius as 'buy'.

text.p: Hungarian hotel group Danubius is poised for further growth following the acquisition of Hungaria Szalloda Rt, K&H Securities said on Monday, rating the stocks a 'buy.'
"Danubius is now a leader among the shares we offer to our clients to buy," analyst Robert Rethy said in a report.

"The company is the top player in the hotel industry and the acquisition of HungarHotels (Hungaria Szalloda) can be considered as a great challenge for the management which certainly pushes Danubius into a new stage of growth."
On Monday, as the Hungarian share market began to recover from last week's falls, Danubius gained more than two percent in early trade.
At 1042 GMT Danubius shares traded at 4,700 forints, above the opening level of 4,500 forints and above Friday's close of 4,600.

Danubius acquired an 85 percent stake, a nominal 4.675 billion forints, in Hungaria and paid 8.125 billion forints. The Competition Office cleared the deal in December and Danubius took up loans totalling 75 million German marks to pay.
K&H Securities expected both Danubius and Hungaria to increase their profits, but said the loan will its leave Danubius in the red as far as its financial activity is concerned.
"According to our estimate Danubius may report a net profit of 3.2 billion forints on a consolidated basis in 1997," Rethy said. In 1996 Danubius had a group pre-tax profit of 2.66 billion.

"Although both Danubius group's and HungarHotels' profitability are expected to increase, the financial burden of the 75 million German marks...is going to lead to losses in financial activity," he said.
But K&H Securities, wholly-owned by Kereskedelmi es Hitelbank (K&H Bank), said it expected the integration to go smoothly.

"Danubius's expertise in operating hotels makes us believe that the integration process is going to be smooth, although the traditionally strong emphasis on spa hotels is likely to be shifted to more general hotel operation," Rethy said.

For 1997 K&H Securities expected Danubius to boost its EPS by some 30 percent to 400 forints and said that 1998 might prove to be an even more successful year after the full integration and flotation of Hungaria.
